 CAB seeks action against LPG overpricing
 BERC public hearing on prices today 
 Published : 29 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 29 October 2026, 00:35
 • 
 ECONOMY
 SHARE 
 Star Business Report 
 File photo 
 The Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) yesterday called for strict action, including licence cancellations, against liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) operators, distributors and retailers found selling cylinders above regulated prices.
 In a statement, the consumer rights body urged the authorities to investigate allegations of artificial shortages, hoarding and overcharging and take effective action against those responsible.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Ahead of the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission’s (BERC) public hearing on LPG prices today, CAB said ensuring sales at regulated prices should take priority over any further increase in prices or related charges.
 Consumers are reportedly paying Tk 500 to Tk 600 more than the fixed price for a 12-kilogramme (kg) cylinder, adding to the financial pressure on low- and middle-income households, it said.
 On October 4, the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder was raised by Tk 252 to Tk 1,837.
 CAB demanded strict enforcement of regulated LPG prices, including licence cancellations for violators, and greater transparency in import, storage, bottling and distribution costs to prevent unjustified charges from burdening consumers
 CAB warned that approving further price increases without first ensuring compliance with regulated prices would place an even greater burden on households that depend on LPG for cooking.
 The association also called for importers’ claims of rising costs to be verified against actual transaction documents and audited accounts.
 It said higher international LPG prices do not necessarily mean local transport, storage and distribution costs rise at the same rate. Higher import costs alone should not justify increases in charges and commissions at every stage of the supply chain.
 Consumers should not have to pay twice for the same expense or bear costs arising from poor management, CAB said.
 The association urged BERC not to approve higher charges or commissions unless audited accounts and independent technical assessments establish that they are necessary. It also called for unjustified costs and excessive profits to be excluded from the pricing formula.
 CAB further demanded separate disclosure of import costs and charges for storage, bottling and distribution. Any benefits from falling international LPG prices should also be passed on to consumers promptly.
 To improve transparency, the association urged the authorities to require all LPG sales outlets to display updated price lists and issue receipts. It also called for clear rules on home delivery and transport charges to prevent unauthorised collections.
 CAB also sought an accessible complaint system to address overcharging, cylinder shortages, underweight cylinders and safety concerns, with complaints resolved within a fixed timeframe.
